description.value:
The following modifications are catalogued alphabetically; any listed prerequisite must already be met when you install one, and you may install a modification the same moment you meet its prerequisites.

  • Advanced Battle Enhancement (requires 15th level and Prototype Battle Enhancement): while playing your Song of Battle, your tech powers and class features ignore resistance to sonic damage, and creatures within range who can hear you treat immunity to sonic damage as resistance instead; additionally, your Battle Song Enhancement feature now creates a fourth burst.
  • Advanced Disruption Enhancement (requires 15th level and Prototype Disruption Enhancement): while playing your Song of Disruption, any hostile creature within range who can hear you must succeed on a Constitution save at the end of each of its turns to maintain concentration on a power.
  • Advanced Support Enhancement (requires 15th level and Prototype Support Enhancement): while playing your Song of Support, allies add your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1) to their death saving throws, and if this would raise the d20 roll to 20 or higher, the creature also regains 1 hit point.
  • Battle Song Enhancement (requires 5th level): while playing your Song of Battle, you can use an action to make two ranged power attacks (against the same target or different ones, each rolled separately), with a range equal to your song's radius, dealing 1d8 sonic damage on a hit.
  • Disruption Song Enhancement (requires 5th level): while playing your Song of Disruption, you can use an action to force a number of creatures within range who can hear you and who are concentrating on a power, up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one), to make a Concentration save; if at least one loses concentration this way, you can use your reaction to deal damage equal to your Intelligence modifier to every creature that did.
  • Enthralling Performance (requires 13th level and Hypnotic Melody): for the duration of an enhanced song, the first time each turn a creature that can hear it tries to attack you, it must succeed on a Charisma save or be unable to attack you this turn (choosing a new target or wasting the attack); on a success it may attack, but has disadvantage on its next save against your powers or features on your following turn. Usable once per long rest.
  • Finding My Way (requires Rush): while playing an enhanced song, when a creature would make a melee attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to move 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks, imposing disadvantage on that roll. Usable twice, with an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level, all restored after a short or long rest.
  • Hypnotic Melody: as an action while wielding your instrument, you begin a subtly hypnotic song; choose creatures up to your Intelligence modifier who, after listening for a full minute, must succeed on a Wisdom save or become charmed by you for 1 minute. Those who succeed never realize you tried, and those who fail also forget once the effect ends. Usable once per short or long rest.
  • Inaudible Casting (requires 7th level and Simple Melodies): casting a tech power or using a feature that requires playing your instrument can be done quietly, giving Intelligence (Investigation) and Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sound disadvantage to detect it.
  • Long Range Noise (requires 13th level): your song's radius extends to 120 feet, and any tech power cast with your instrument that deals sonic damage and has a range of 10 feet or more gains a range of 120 feet.
  • Magnifying Device (requires 5th level): while using your instrument as a tech focus, +1 to tech attack rolls, rising to +2 at 9th level and +3 at 13th level.
  • Overwhelming Soundwaves (requires 15th level): while playing, creatures of your choice treat a 15-foot-radius sphere around you as difficult terrain; as an action, each affected creature must succeed on a Constitution save or take 3d8 sonic damage.
  • Prototype Battle Enhancement (requires 9th level and Battle Song Enhancement): while playing your Song of Battle, casting a tech power or using a feature that affects others within your song's radius lets you choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the power's level to automatically succeed on their saves and take no damage where a success would otherwise deal half; additionally, your Battle Song Enhancement feature now creates a third burst.
  • Prototype Disruption Enhancement (requires 9th level and Disruption Song Enhancement): while playing your Song of Disruption, when a creature you see who can hear you attempts to cast a power, you can use your reaction to cast tech override at 3rd level, working against both tech and force powers and adding your proficiency bonus to the techcasting ability check for that casting. Usable once per short or long rest.
  • Prototype Support Enhancement (requires 9th level and Support Song Enhancement): while playing your Song of Support, using your Potent Amplitude benefit means the target takes no damage on a successful save and only half on a failed one.
  • Restful Melody: over a short rest, you can play a rejuvenating song; if you or any friendly creature who heard the performance regains hit points at the end of that rest, it also regains an extra 1d6 hit points. This bonus grows to 1d8 at 9th level, 1d10 at 13th level, and 1d12 at 17th level.
  • Rush: while playing an enhanced song, your speed increases by 10 feet, and opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage.
  • Sharp Noise: as an action while wielding your instrument, choose a creature you can see; if it can hear you, it must succeed on a Constitution save or take 1d4 sonic damage and have disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn. This damage grows to 2d4 at 5th level, 3d4 at 11th level, and 4d4 at 17th level.
  • Shock Mount (requires 5th level): while using your instrument as a tech focus, +1 to your tech save DC, rising to +2 at 9th level and +3 at 13th level.
  • Simple Melodies: while holding your instrument without actively playing a song, any tech power you could cast whose damage type your Potent Amplitude feature could alter may be cast as though you were using Potent Amplitude. Usable twice, with an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level, all restored after a short or long rest.
  • Sonar Pulse: as an action while wielding your instrument, you release a wave of sound that reads your surroundings, granting advantage for 1 minute on Wisdom (Perception) and Intelligence (Investigation) checks to find hidden doors, traps, or invisible creatures. Usable once per short or long rest.
  • Song Flow (requires 11th level): while playing an enhanced song, you can use a bonus action to switch to a different song.
  • Support Song Enhancement (requires 5th level): while playing your Song of Support, a tech power you cast that restores hit points or grants temporary hit points restores or grants an extra amount equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1).
  • Weapon Integration: you can build a single weapon of 8 pounds or less into your instrument, giving it the hidden property.
